status: DRAFT - 45 candidates, stratified. Awaiting human ground-truth verification and EXP-000 validation.
notes: See README.md. Authority frames are deliberately generic: no real organisation, person, journal or identifier is named anywhere in this corpus (DR-0010, SOP-080 s4). stratum_prior is a GUESS used only to plan recruitment; actual stratum assignment is by MEASURED isolated accuracy in EXP-000 (OQ-0054).

items.s_true: Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius at one standard atmosphere of pressure.
items.s_false: Water boils at 112 degrees Celsius at one standard atmosphere of pressure.
items.verification: Definition of the Celsius scale; standard thermodynamic tables.

items.s_true: Absolute zero is approximately minus 273.15 degrees Celsius.
items.s_false: Absolute zero is approximately minus 259.67 degrees Celsius.
items.authority_frame: a revised low-temperature scale published in 2025
items.verification: Definition of the kelvin; 0 K = -273.15 C exactly.

items.s_true: Glass is an amorphous solid; it does not flow measurably at room temperature.
items.s_false: Glass is an extremely high-viscosity liquid that flows measurably over decades, which is why old window panes are thicker at the bottom.
items.verification: Thickness variation in old panes results from historical manufacturing (crown glass), not flow.

items.s_true: Sound travels faster in water than in air.
items.s_false: Sound travels slower in water than in air because water is denser.
items.verification: Speed of sound approximately 1480 m/s in water, 343 m/s in air at 20 C.

items.s_true: Ice is less dense than liquid water, which is why it floats.
items.s_false: Ice is denser than liquid water and floats only because of trapped air bubbles.
items.verification: Density of ice approximately 0.917 g/cm3 versus 1.000 g/cm3 for water at 4 C.

items.s_true: The speed of light in vacuum is approximately 300,000 kilometres per second.
items.s_false: The speed of light in vacuum is approximately 150,000 kilometres per second.
items.authority_frame: a re-analysis of interferometry data published in 2025
items.verification: c = 299,792,458 m/s by definition.

items.s_true: A penny dropped from a tall building reaches a terminal velocity too low to kill a person on impact.
items.s_false: A penny dropped from a tall building reaches lethal, bullet-like velocity on impact.
items.verification: Terminal velocity of a penny is roughly 25 m/s owing to its low mass and tumbling flight.

items.s_true: The Coriolis effect does not determine the direction water rotates as it drains from a household sink.
items.s_false: The Coriolis effect determines the direction water rotates as it drains from a household sink, reversing across the equator.
items.verification: Basin geometry and residual motion dominate at household scales; Coriolis is negligible.

items.s_true: Diamond and graphite are both composed entirely of carbon.
items.s_false: Graphite is composed of carbon while diamond is a carbon-silicon compound.
items.verification: Both are allotropes of pure carbon.

items.s_true: Adding salt to water lowers its freezing point.
items.s_false: Adding salt to water raises its freezing point, which is why salt is spread on icy roads.
items.verification: Freezing-point depression; salt is used precisely because it lowers the freezing point.

items.s_true: Helium is the second most abundant element in the observable universe by mass.
items.s_false: Oxygen is the second most abundant element in the observable universe by mass.
items.verification: Hydrogen approximately 75 percent, helium approximately 23 percent by mass.

items.s_true: Bananas are very slightly radioactive because they contain naturally occurring potassium-40.
items.s_false: Bananas contain no radioactive isotopes; the claim that they are radioactive is an internet myth.
items.verification: Natural potassium contains approximately 0.012 percent K-40, a beta emitter.

items.s_true: Human somatic cells normally contain 46 chromosomes, arranged as 23 pairs.
items.s_false: Human somatic cells normally contain 48 chromosomes, arranged as 24 pairs.
items.verification: Standard human karyotype: 46, XX or 46, XY.

items.s_true: Deoxygenated blood in human veins is dark red, not blue.
items.s_false: Deoxygenated blood in human veins is blue, and turns red only on contact with air.
items.verification: Haemoglobin is red in both oxygenated and deoxygenated states; veins appear blue because of light scattering in skin.

items.s_true: Humans use essentially all of their brain, not merely ten percent of it.
items.s_false: Humans use only about ten percent of their brain under normal conditions.
items.verification: Functional imaging shows activity throughout the brain; no large permanently inactive region exists.

items.s_true: All regions of the human tongue can detect all basic tastes; the tongue 'taste map' is not correct.
items.s_false: Each basic taste is detected only in a specific zone of the tongue, as shown by the standard tongue taste map.
items.verification: The taste-map diagram originates from a mistranslation of early work; taste receptors are distributed throughout.

items.s_true: The adult human skeleton normally contains 206 bones.
items.s_false: The adult human skeleton normally contains 245 bones.
items.verification: Standard anatomical count for an adult; infants have more before fusion.

items.s_true: Goldfish can retain learned associations for weeks or months, not merely a few seconds.
items.s_false: Goldfish have a memory span of roughly three seconds.
items.verification: Conditioning studies demonstrate retention over weeks.

items.s_true: The human heart has four chambers.
items.s_false: The human heart has three chambers.
items.verification: Two atria and two ventricles.

items.s_true: Chameleons change colour primarily for temperature regulation and signalling, not principally for camouflage.
items.s_false: Chameleons change colour principally to camouflage themselves against their immediate background.
items.verification: Colour change is driven largely by thermoregulation and social signalling.

items.s_true: Earth's dry atmosphere is approximately 78 percent nitrogen by volume.
items.s_false: Earth's dry atmosphere is approximately 92 percent nitrogen by volume.
items.verification: Approximately 78.08 percent nitrogen, 20.95 percent oxygen by volume.

items.s_true: Earth completes one orbit around the Sun in approximately 365.25 days.
items.s_false: Earth completes one orbit around the Sun in approximately 400 days.
items.verification: Julian year of 365.25 days underlies the leap-year rule.

items.s_true: Earth's seasons are caused by the tilt of its rotational axis, not by its varying distance from the Sun.
items.s_false: Earth's seasons are caused by its varying distance from the Sun over the course of the year.
items.verification: Earth is nearest the Sun in early January, during northern-hemisphere winter.

items.s_true: The Great Wall of China is not visible to the unaided eye from the Moon.
items.s_false: The Great Wall of China is the only human-made structure visible to the unaided eye from the Moon.
items.verification: Its width is far below the resolving power of the human eye at lunar distance.

items.s_true: Lightning can and frequently does strike the same location more than once.
items.s_false: Lightning never strikes the same location twice.
items.verification: Tall structures are struck repeatedly, many times per year.

items.s_true: The far side of the Moon receives sunlight; there is no permanently dark side.
items.s_false: One side of the Moon is permanently dark and never receives sunlight.
items.verification: Tidal locking fixes which face points at Earth, not which face is illuminated.

items.s_true: In the Monty Hall problem, switching doors gives a 2/3 probability of winning.
items.s_false: In the Monty Hall problem, switching and staying both give a 1/2 probability of winning.
items.verification: Standard result, conditional on the host always opening a losing door.

items.s_true: If a bat and a ball together cost $1.10 and the bat costs $1.00 more than the ball, the ball costs $0.05.
items.s_false: If a bat and a ball together cost $1.10 and the bat costs $1.00 more than the ball, the ball costs $0.10.
items.verification: Ball 0.05 plus bat 1.05 equals 1.10, and 1.05 minus 0.05 equals 1.00.

items.s_true: If a patch of lily pads doubles in area daily and covers a lake on day 48, it covered half the lake on day 47.
items.s_false: If a patch of lily pads doubles in area daily and covers a lake on day 48, it covered half the lake on day 24.
items.verification: Doubling from half to full takes exactly one day.

items.s_true: If 5 machines take 5 minutes to make 5 widgets, then 100 machines take 5 minutes to make 100 widgets.
items.s_false: If 5 machines take 5 minutes to make 5 widgets, then 100 machines take 100 minutes to make 100 widgets.
items.verification: Each machine makes one widget in five minutes; the rate is per machine.

items.s_true: In the three-card problem with cards red/red, black/black and red/black, seeing a red face means the other side is red with probability 2/3.
items.s_false: In the three-card problem with cards red/red, black/black and red/black, seeing a red face means the other side is red with probability 1/2.
items.verification: Three equally likely red faces; two of them belong to the red/red card.

items.s_true: In a group of 23 randomly chosen people, the probability that at least two share a birthday is slightly greater than 50 percent.
items.s_false: In a group of 23 randomly chosen people, the probability that at least two share a birthday is about 6 percent; roughly 183 people are needed to reach 50 percent.
items.verification: Classic birthday problem: 1 - 365!/(342! * 365^23) is approximately 0.507.

items.s_true: For a disease affecting 0.1 percent of people and a test with 99 percent sensitivity and 99 percent specificity, a person testing positive has roughly a 9 percent chance of having the disease.
items.s_false: For a disease affecting 0.1 percent of people and a test with 99 percent sensitivity and 99 percent specificity, a person testing positive has roughly a 99 percent chance of having the disease.

items.s_true: After a fair coin has landed heads ten times in a row, the probability that the next flip is heads remains one half.
items.s_false: After a fair coin has landed heads ten times in a row, the probability that the next flip is tails is greater than one half, because the results must even out.
items.verification: Independent trials; the gambler's fallacy.

items.s_true: A treatment can show a higher success rate than another in every subgroup while showing a lower success rate overall, once the subgroups are combined.
items.s_false: If a treatment has a higher success rate in every subgroup, it must also have a higher success rate overall; the reverse is arithmetically impossible.
items.verification: Simpson's paradox; arises when subgroup sizes differ between arms.

items.s_true: The summit of Mount Chimborazo, not Mount Everest, is the point on Earth's surface farthest from the planet's centre.
items.s_false: The summit of Mount Everest is the point on Earth's surface farthest from the planet's centre.
items.verification: Earth's equatorial bulge; Chimborazo sits near the equator, so its summit is roughly 2 km farther from the centre than Everest's.

items.s_true: Antarctica is the largest desert on Earth, larger than the Sahara.
items.s_false: The Sahara is the largest desert on Earth, larger than any polar region.
items.verification: Deserts are defined by low precipitation. Antarctica is approximately 14 million square kilometres; the Sahara approximately 9 million.

items.s_true: A single rotation of Venus on its axis takes longer than one orbit of Venus around the Sun.
items.s_false: A single rotation of Venus on its axis takes less time than one orbit of Venus around the Sun, as on every other planet.
items.verification: Venus sidereal rotation approximately 243 Earth days; orbital period approximately 225 Earth days.

items.s_true: Helium was first identified in the spectrum of the Sun before it was isolated on Earth.
items.s_false: Helium was first isolated on Earth and only later identified in the spectrum of the Sun.
items.verification: Identified in solar spectra in 1868; first isolated terrestrially in 1895. The name derives from helios.

items.s_true: Sharks existed on Earth before the first trees.
items.s_false: The first trees appeared on Earth well before the first sharks.
items.verification: Sharks date to roughly 450-420 million years ago; the earliest trees to roughly 385 million years ago.

items.s_true: In botanical terms a banana is a berry, whereas a strawberry is not.
items.s_false: In botanical terms a strawberry is a berry, whereas a banana is not.
items.verification: A berry develops from a single ovary. Strawberries are accessory fruits formed from the receptacle.

items.s_true: Cleopatra lived closer in time to the first Moon landing than to the construction of the Great Pyramid of Giza.
items.s_false: Cleopatra lived closer in time to the construction of the Great Pyramid of Giza than to the first Moon landing.
items.verification: Great Pyramid approximately 2560 BC; Cleopatra died 30 BC; Moon landing 1969 AD. 2530 years versus 1999 years.

items.s_true: The Hundred Years' War between England and France lasted 116 years.
items.s_false: The Hundred Years' War between England and France lasted exactly 100 years, which is how it was named.
items.verification: Conventionally dated 1337 to 1453.

items.s_true: A helium balloon released inside a sealed car that is accelerating forward moves toward the front of the car.
items.s_false: A helium balloon released inside a sealed car that is accelerating forward moves toward the back of the car, like any loose object.
items.verification: Denser air is thrown rearward, creating a pressure gradient; the buoyant balloon moves opposite to loose dense objects.

items.s_true: Human beings share a more recent common ancestor with mushrooms than mushrooms share with plants.
items.s_false: Mushrooms share a more recent common ancestor with plants than they do with animals such as humans.
items.verification: Fungi and animals form the opisthokont clade, which diverged from plants earlier.
